chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Malik, from Abu Qatada, from Sahl ibn al-Yasa'

that when Sahl established Sahlabad, he asked Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) about what was to be taken from it, what was obligated upon him. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If the Sultan takes its tax (kharaj), then there is nothing upon you; and if the Sultan does not take anything from it, then upon you is the payment of the tenth (ushr) of whatever is in it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the obligation of paying khums or ushr if the government has already collected land tax?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of 'doubt resolution' in fiscal jurisprudence, establishing that the religious obligation of the tenth (ushr) is suspended if the secular ruler (Sultan) has already appropriated the land tax (kharaj). It highlights the Shia scholarly distinction between state exactions and divine dues, ensuring believers are not burdened with double taxation when the authority's claim is established. This ruling underscores the flexibility of Islamic law in accommodating varying administrative practices of the ruling power.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Abdullah Bin Malik, from Abu Qatada,

(It has been narrated) from Sahl Bin Al-Yas’a when he established Sahl Abaad, and asked Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup> about what to take from it, what was (Obligated) upon him. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If it was so that the Sultan (ruling authority) has taken its taxes, so there is nothing upon you; and if the Sultan (ruling authority) has not taken anything from it, so upon you is its tax of a tenth (10%), whatever happens to be in it’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ‘Abd Allah ibn Malik from abu Qatadah from Sahl ibn al- Yasa’

who after establishing Sahl Abad asked abu al-Hassan Musa, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, the following: “Sahl once asked abu al-Hassan, Musa, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about what he pays to al-Sultan (the ruler). He (the Imam) said, ‘If al-Sultan (the ruler) receives its Kharaj (taxes) there is not anything on you; but if al-Sultan (the ruler) does not receive anything, then you pay one out of ten of whatever is due.’”
